newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. says will be flexible on WTO infotech deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says will be flexible on WTO infotech deal.

text.p: The United States is prepared to show flexibility in trying to win a deal at the World Trade Organisation meeting this week to eliminate tariffs on information technology, a senior U.S. trade official said Monday.

"We're prepared to show the necessary flexibility to get a deal done here," Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang said at a news conference. "A deal will obviously require a commitment from Europe as well."
The United States has been pushing to win a deal on an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) by the time the first meeting of WTO ministers ends on Friday.
"We strongly feel that if we don't get an ITA here, there is a serious risk that we may not be able to get it at any time. That is why we are pushing so hard here," Lang said.

The United States has accused the European Union of dragging its feet on the agreement, but EU officials have pointed to the Americans' desire to exclude four products -- capacitors, graphics tubes, photocopiers and fibre optics. Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and European Union Trade
Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan met on Monday afternoon to try to work out their differences and planned to meet again later in the evening.
Lang said the meeting lasted about an hour and "provided a basis for moving forward". But he added that there was "still a lot of difficult work to do".
